facts.fact_text: The applicant was at the material time the Deputy General Prosecutor of Armenia.
The applicant had occupied the post of Deputy General Prosecutor of Armenia since 17 January 2006.
The applicant held the rank of First Category State Justice Councillor.

Immediately after the announcement of the preliminary results of the 19 February 2008 presidential election, Mr Ter-Petrosyan called on his supporters to gather at Freedom Square in central Yerevan in order to protest against alleged irregularities in the election process.
Mr Ter-Petrosyan announced that the 19 February 2008 presidential election had not been free and fair.
From 20 February 2008 onwards, nationwide daily protest rallies were held by Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters.
The main meeting place of Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters during the protest rallies was Freedom Square and the surrounding park in Yerevan.
The rallies at Freedom Square attracted at times tens of thousands of people.
Several hundred demonstrators stayed in the Freedom Square area around the clock, having set up a camp.
On 22 February 2008 the applicant made a speech at the rally held at Freedom Square.
In his speech at Freedom Square on 22 February 2008, the applicant expressed his support for Mr Ter-Petrosyan.
In his speech at Freedom Square on 22 February 2008, the applicant criticised the conduct of the presidential election, alleging various types of irregularities.
In his speech at Freedom Square on 22 February 2008, the applicant called on those gathered not to give up and to stand by their votes.
In his speech at Freedom Square on 22 February 2008, the applicant said that rule of law had to be finally established in Armenia.
On 22 February 2008, the same date as the applicant's speech at Freedom Square, the General Prosecutor applied to the President of Armenia seeking to have the applicant dismissed.
On 23 February 2008 the President of Armenia issued a decree dismissing the applicant from the post of Deputy General Prosecutor.
On 23 February 2008 the President of Armenia issued a decree depriving the applicant of his rank of First Category State Justice Councillor.
According to the applicant, on 23 February 2008 at around 10 p.m. the applicant, his brother V.J., and four others had been travelling from Ejmiatsin to Yerevan in two cars.
According to the applicant, after stopping at the intersection near Argavand village, the applicant and his companions had been attacked by a group of masked and armed persons.
According to the applicant, the masked and armed persons had crashed their unmarked vehicle into the front of the applicant's car.
According to the applicant, the masked and armed persons had come out of their vehicle and, firing their guns, had surrounded the applicant's car.
According to the applicant, the applicant had surrendered himself and his weapon to the masked and armed persons and had been taken into their car.
According to the applicant, the applicant, his brother V.J. and two others, together with their cars, were taken into police custody.

According to an announcement made on 23 February 2008 on the website of the Armenian police entitled 'Gagik Jhangiryan is in custody', operative information had been received at the Principal Department for the Fight against Organised Crime (PDFOC) that the persons driving two cars (with indication of licence plates) had been armed and intended to destabilise the situation in Yerevan.
According to the Armenian police announcement, at around 11 p.m. on 23 February 2008 the above-mentioned cars had been pulled over near Argavand intersection by PDFOC officers.
According to the Armenian police announcement, during an inspection near Argavand intersection, PDFOC officers encountered resistance from the persons in the cars.

According to the Armenian police announcement, as a result of the resistance encountered near Argavand intersection, one of the police officers had accidentally fired his service gun, inflicting light injuries on two other police officers and V.J., who had put up resistance.
According to the Armenian police announcement, the persons in question, including the applicant, V.J. and two other persons accompanying them, had been taken to the PDFOC.
According to the Armenian police announcement, a CZ-75-type pistol had been found in the applicant's possession.
According to the Armenian police announcement, two other pistols had been found in the possession of V.J. and one of the other two persons accompanying the applicant.

According to the record of bringing a person in, the applicant was brought in to the PDFOC on suspicion of illegal possession, carrying and transportation of arms and ammunition, and for showing resistance to police officers.
The applicant alleged that police officers had thrown him and his brother V.J. to the ground and started kicking and punching them in the lobby of the PDFOC.
The applicant alleged that when he had pleaded with the police officers not to hit V.J. because of his spinal disease, they had started hitting V.J. even more vigorously, aiming at his spine.
Officers A.H. and T.A. described how the applicant had refused to step out of the car and how they had had to apply force in order to take him inside the PDFOC building.

Officers A.H. and T.A. described how the applicant had punched officer A.H., torn officer T.A.'s uniform, used swear words and made threats during the process of being taken inside the PDFOC building.
On 27 February 2008 at 3.30 a.m. the applicant was brought before the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan decided to allow the investigator's application for the applicant's detention.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that the circumstances of the case and the evidence obtained provided sufficient reasons to believe that, if the applicant remained at large, he could commit a new offence, abscond or obstruct the proceedings.
On 7 March 2008 the Criminal Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal against the detention decision.
The Criminal Court of Appeal found on 7 March 2008 that there was a reasonable suspicion, from the materials submitted, that the applicant had committed the imputed offences.
The Criminal Court of Appeal found on 7 March 2008 that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan's decision to detain the applicant was well-reasoned.

On 23 April 2008 the applicant lodged an appeal against the extension of his detention, arguing inter alia that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan's decision was unreasoned and the risks of his absconding or obstructing the investigation were unsubstantiated.

On 8 May 2008 the Criminal Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal against the extension of his detention, finding that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan's decision to extend the applicant's detention was well-reasoned.
On 19 June 2008 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan extended the applicant's detention by two more months.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan, in extending the applicant's detention on 19 June 2008, took into account the nature and gravity of the imputed offences.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found on 19 June 2008 that, if the applicant remained at large, he could abscond, obstruct the proceedings by exerting pressure on the persons involved in the proceedings and, by his actions, hinder the further disclosure of the circumstances of the case.
On 2 July 2008 the Criminal Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal against the extension of his detention.
The Criminal Court of Appeal found on 2 July 2008 that there was a reasonable suspicion from the materials submitted that the applicant had committed an offence.
The Criminal Court of Appeal found on 2 July 2008 that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan's decision to extend the applicant's detention was well-reasoned.
On 23 March 2009 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan sentenced the applicant to three years' imprisonment.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that on 23 February 2008 at around 11.30 p.m. the applicant, having been brought in to the courtyard of the PDFOC upon a suspicion of carrying illegal firearms and ammunition, disobeyed the lawful orders of police officers who were performing their official duties.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant punched and caused pain to police officer A.H.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant pulled and tore the uniform of officer T.A., refused to enter the PDFOC building and threatened the police officers and their families with physical retribution.
On 22 February 2008, the same date as the applicant's speech at Freedom Square, the General Prosecutor applied to the President of Armenia seeking to have the applicant dismissed.

The General Prosecutor's application to the President of Armenia sought the applicant's dismissal on the ground that the applicant had participated in a rally and made a political speech, thereby violating the law which required prosecutors to maintain political neutrality and not to engage in political activities.
On 23 February 2008 the President of Armenia issued a decree dismissing the applicant from the post of Deputy General Prosecutor.
On 23 February 2008 the President of Armenia issued a decree depriving the applicant of his rank of First Category State Justice Councillor.

According to the record of bringing a person in, the applicant was brought in to the PDFOC on suspicion of illegal possession, carrying and transportation of arms and ammunition, and for showing resistance to police officers.

The record of the applicant's arrest stated that the applicant was arrested on suspicion of illegal acquisition, possession and carrying of arms and ammunition, as provided for by Article 235 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.
The record of the applicant's arrest stated that on 23 February 2008 a CZ-75 B-type pistol had been found in the applicant's possession, together with 14 cartridges.

Later on 24 February 2008 another criminal case was instituted under Article 235 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (illegal acquisition, possession or carrying of arms and ammunition) in respect of the applicant.
The second criminal case instituted under Article 235 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code was joined with the first criminal case.
The second criminal case alleged that the applicant, in unknown circumstances, had illegally acquired from an unidentified person a Browning-type pistol loaded with 9 mm cartridges.

The second criminal case alleged that the applicant had illegally kept the Browning-type pistol in the VAZ 21010 car accompanying him on 23 February 2008, which had later been found during the inspection of that car.
On 26 February 2008 the applicant was formally charged under Article 235 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (illegal acquisition, possession or carrying of arms and ammunition).
On 26 February 2008 the applicant was formally charged under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (non-life or health-threatening assault on a public official).

As regards the charge under Article 235 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code, it was stated that the applicant, under circumstances yet to be disclosed, had illegally obtained a firearm, namely a 9 mm Browning pistol together with its cartridges, which he had illegally kept in the car accompanying him.

As regards the charge under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code, it was stated that, after being taken to the PDFOC on suspicion of illegally carrying a firearm, the applicant, while in the courtyard of the PDFOC building, had disobeyed the lawful orders of PDFOC officers to step out of the police car and to enter the building.
As regards the charge under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code, it was stated that the applicant had punched officer A.H. in the shoulder, as a result of which the officer had fallen down.
As regards the charge under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code, it was stated that the applicant had pulled and torn the uniform of officer T.A.

As regards the charge under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code, it was stated that the applicant had refused to enter the PDFOC building and threatened the officers with violence and retribution.
On 13 June 2008 a new charge was brought against the applicant under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (usurpation of power).

The new charge under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code alleged that the applicant, following the 19 February 2008 presidential election, had joined Levon Ter-Petrosyan and his followers in masterminding and taking actions seeking to usurp power.

The new charge under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code alleged that the applicant, using his standing as Deputy General Prosecutor, had participated in discrediting the conduct of the election, casting doubt on its lawfulness among the international community, and instilling distrust towards the results among large segments of the population.

The new charge under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code alleged that the applicant had created illusions of public discontent and revolt, and organised and conducted unlawful mass rallies aimed at destabilising the political situation in Armenia.

The new charge under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code alleged that the applicant had planned and taken actions seeking to isolate lawful public officials, force them to resign and exercise power in their stead.
The new charge under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code alleged that the applicant had made public speeches and calls of a provocative nature aimed at usurping state power.

The Explanatory Memorandum to the Report on the Functioning of Democratic Institutions in Armenia (Doc. 11579), produced by the co-rapporteurs, stated that the opposition received a boost in support when a number of high-level state officials publicly denounced the 19 February 2008 presidential election as fraudulent and announced their support for Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan.

The Explanatory Memorandum to the Report on the Functioning of Democratic Institutions in Armenia (Doc. 11579) stated that those high-level state officials who publicly denounced the election were subsequently dismissed from their positions.

The Explanatory Memorandum to the Report on the Functioning of Democratic Institutions in Armenia (Doc. 11579) stated that a number of those high-level state officials, as well as several opposition activists, were arrested on seemingly artificial charges, which left the impression that their prosecution was politically motivated.

The Explanatory Memorandum to the Report on the Functioning of Democratic Institutions in Armenia (Doc. 11579) stated that according to the Helsinki Association of Armenia, a total of 14 persons were arrested and placed under investigation in the period from 20 to 29 February 2008.

Between April 2008 and June 2009 the OSCE/ODIHR (Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe/Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights) conducted a monitoring project of about a hundred trials of opposition leaders and supporters related to the events of 1-2 March 2008.
The OSCE/ODIHR monitoring project of trials related to the events of 1-2 March 2008 included the applicant's case under number 94.
